name: Early-onset Calcifying Leukoencephalopathy with Skeletal Dysplasia
aliases: Early-onset Calcifying Leukoencephalopathy and Skeletal Dysplasia Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Early-onset Calcifying Leukoencephalopathy-Skeletal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral symmetrical intracranial calcifications predominantly affecting the white matter on neuroimaging
Radiological evidence of skeletal dysplasia including metaphyseal irregularities and abnormal bone modeling
Onset of neurological symptoms such as developmental delay or hypotonia within the first two years of life
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with calcifying leukoencephalopathy and skeletal dysplasia (if available)
Exclusion of infectious, metabolic, or other genetic causes of intracranial calcifications and skeletal abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: bilateral intracranial calcifications affecting white matter, radiological skeletal dysplasia, and early-onset neurological symptoms
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended but not mandatory for diagnosis. Differential diagnoses must be carefully excluded.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bilateral symmetrical intracranial white matter calcifications
pathognomonic.notes: Detected by CT or MRI imaging
searchTerms: symmetrical calcium deposits in brain white matter
intracranial white matter calcium buildup on both sides

pathognomonic.symptomName: Radiological skeletal dysplasia with metaphyseal irregularities
searchTerms: abnormal bone growth with irregular metaphyses

pathognomonic.notes: Typically presenting within first 2 years of life

common.notes: Limited joint mobility due to fibrosis or dysplasia

occasional.notes: Head circumference below normal for age

rare.notes: Sensorineural hearing loss reported in some cases

laboratory: Normal to mildly elevated inflammatory markers
Normal metabolic screening excluding other causes
imaging: CT showing bilateral symmetrical calcifications in cerebral white matter
Skeletal X-rays demonstrating metaphyseal irregularities and bone dysplasia
MRI may show white matter abnormalities and calcifications
other: Exclusion of infectious causes such as TORCH infections
Negative metabolic and mitochondrial disease workup

distinguishingFeatures: Cortical calcifications rather than white matter
Calcifications often periventricular and basal ganglia

redFlags: Progressive skeletal deformities with functional impairment
Early onset seizures refractory to treatment
